## UNBLOCKED — the stash research that gated this is complete

This ticket was held pending research into how OSS projects handle the shared-stash hazard under
worktrees, because its fix and that question touch the same held-out-oracle workflow. That research
is done and filed as **tasteful-euhedral-bilby (40e3-625b-de1a-42ff)**. Two results bear directly on
this ticket:

**1. `git stash create` silently drops UNTRACKED files** — and `-u` accepts the flag and still
does not capture them (verified on git 2.55: the stash commit has only two parents). A held-out
oracle is typically a newly authored, untracked test file, so `stash create` is a silent
data-loss trap for exactly that case. Do not reach for it here.

**2. The recommended substitute is a MOVE, not a stash**: `mv <file> "$(git rev-parse --git-path
heldout)/"` and move it back. Zero git involvement, so zero shared-ref surface; identical for
tracked and untracked files; per-worktree and auto-cleaned with the worktree. The requirement is
that the oracle be ABSENT FROM THE FILESYSTEM, which a move does directly and a stash only
incidentally.

**Scope note:** this ticket is about the nested-pytest launch that evades the uniqueness guard and
destroys other sessions' shared temp roots. It is NOT the stash ticket. Keep them separate — but if
the fix touches how the held-out file is set aside, use the move pattern above rather than
reintroducing a stash.

Ready to dispatch. file_impact is recorded (`tests/unit/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py`,
`tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py`) and conflicts with nothing currently in flight.

comments.body:
## Change 2656 pushed — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2656

Not submitted, ticket left `in_progress`: the operator verifies votes and submits.

### AC1 — the violator no longer allocates into the shared root

`test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` now routes through `run_nested_pytest`.
The `python -c` payload's `assert 'pydantic_ai.providers.anthropic' not in sys.modules`
was dropped, and that loses nothing: it ran before `pytest.main`, in an interpreter that
had imported only `sys`, so it could not fail. A fresh `python -m pytest` child IS the
condition the test names.

Proof (run under an explicit parent `--basetemp`, so the module's children are the only
thing that could have touched the shared root):

```
--- created ---   (none)
--- DELETED ---   (none)
child basetemps:  .bt/ac1/test_anthropic_auth_oracle_iso{0,1,2,3}/nested-pytest
```

4 passed. Pre-fix the same module created four and deleted four.

### AC2/AC3 — the guard, and the seeded defects

The guard no longer matches one argv shape. It classifies a sequence literal into three
spellings of one operation and applies the admission each one can actually satisfy:

| spelling | detection | admitted by |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest` | argv triple `(sys.executable, "-m", "pytest")` | the helper, or a reasoned marker |
| `python -c <payload naming pytest>` | `(sys.executable, "-c", payload)` where the payload's static text mentions pytest — resolved through the module's string bindings, since the violator bound its payload to a local first, and through f-string literal parts | the helper, or a reasoned marker |
| bare `pytest` console script | argv[0] is `<anything> / "pytest"`, directly or via a local, through a `str()`/`os.fspath()` wrapper | an explicit `--basetemp` in the same literal, or a marker |

The console-script form gets the weaker admission on purpose: it *cannot* use the helper
(`python -m pytest` puts the repo root on the child's `sys.path` and destroys what those
tests reproduce), and the invariant being defended is the child's temp root, not the
helper's monopoly.

Defect seeding, in the real tree, one spelling at a time — `test_the_launch_appears_only_in_the_helper`:

```
baseline (all fixed)                          PASS
seed 1: -c payload (the pre-fix violator)     FAIL
seed 2: console script, --basetemp removed    FAIL
seed 3: the -m triple (regression check)      FAIL
restored                                      PASS
```

Files were set aside by copy under `git rev-parse --git-path heldout`, per the move
pattern in tasteful-euhedral-bilby — no stash was used anywhere.

The pre-fix payload is also kept verbatim in the guard as `_PRE_FIX_VIOLATOR`, so a
revert stays a permanently checked defect rather than one I checked once.

### AC4 — the sweep, and its dispositions

Scanned: every `*.py` under `tests/` (the guard's own tree walk, which is the sweep) plus
a manual grep over `tests/`, `scripts/` and `src/` for `pytest.main`, quoted `pytest`,
`Popen`/`check_output`/`check_call`, and every `"-c"` argv.

| site | spelling | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py:32` | `-c` payload, no basetemp | **fixed here** (AC1) |
| `test_tests_import_convention.py:97` | bare console script, **no basetemp** | **fixed here** — second violator, found by the widened guard, `--basetemp` added under `tmp_path` |
| `test_scripts_import_convention.py:154` | bare console script | already passes `--basetemp`; admitted unchanged |
| `test_mechanism_delta.py:440` | bare console script | already passes `--basetemp`; admitted unchanged |
| `test_error_handling_convention.py:125`, `workflow/test_terraform_plan_review_tools.py:300`, `workflow/test_map_fanout.py:294`, `interfaces/facades/test_mcp_client_configs.py:365` | in-process `pytest.main` | all four are inside `if __name__ == "__main__":`, so they never run during a suite. Not flagged, deliberately. |
| `test_ci_workflow_parity.py:1337` | `stub_bin / "pytest"` | a stub written to disk and put on `PATH`, never argv[0]. Correctly not flagged — verified. |
| `test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py`, `test_repo_isolation_guard.py` | `pytester.runpytest*` | pytest owns their basetemp; out of scope, as `_nested_pytest.py` already records |
| `scripts/run_live_matrix.py:80`, `scripts/mutation_gate.py:579` | build a pytest argv | outside `tests/`, so outside this guard's tree walk. **Not covered — see below.** |

Zero false positives: every other `python -c` payload under `tests/` (~12 sites) stays
unflagged, and two negative-control tests pin that.

### What the guard still cannot see — stated rather than claimed away

- **Anything outside `tests/`.** `scripts/run_live_matrix.py` and `scripts/mutation_gate.py`
  construct pytest argvs; the guard's tree walk is rooted at `tests/`. They are operator
  tooling, not suite children, so they cannot prune a concurrent session's root the way a
  test can — but the guard does not check them and I did not widen its root here.
- **argv assembled incrementally** — `cmd = [sys.executable]` then `cmd += ["-m", "pytest"]`.
  Detection is per sequence literal; no literal contains the triple. Not present in the
  tree today.
- **A console script not at argv[0]** — e.g. `["env", "X=1", str(console_script), ...]`.
  Only argv[0] is checked. Not present today.
- **A `-c` payload that reaches pytest only through an interpolated value**, so no literal
  part of the f-string says "pytest". Not present today.

Each of these is a narrower gap than the one just closed, and each is listed so the next
reader does not have to rediscover that it was a choice.

### Gates and checks

`make lint` rc=0; `make typecheck` rc=0 (762 files). Complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0
stale=16`; mechanism ratchet `new=0 increased=0`. No new mechanism was introduced — the
change reshapes an existing guard rather than adding one.

Verified with the **bare `pytest` console script** throughout, not `python -m pytest`:
`test_tests_import_convention.py` + `test_scripts_import_convention.py` green, and the
five affected modules green (57 passed).

### One transient, recorded not chased

`test_scripts_import_convention.py::test_repro_module_passes_standalone` failed once in a
four-module selection (child rc 1 with "3 passed" in its own output), then passed 4/4 on
re-run with identical selection and `-p no:randomly`. That module is **unmodified by this
change**. Shape matches the same-family transient already noted in this ticket's
description; not investigated further here.

Orchestrator close — acceptance criteria ticked on the implementing agent's REPORTED per-AC
evidence, and the change is merged to `origin/main`.

What I verified myself before ticking:
- the merge commit exists on `origin/main` and carries this ticket's `rebar-ticket:` trailer;
- the commit is reachable from a throwaway worktree checked out at `origin/main`, which is where
  this close is being run (the shared main checkout holds another session's uncommitted work, so
  it was deliberately not fast-forwarded);
- both Gerrit gates were green on the submitted patchset (`LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`).

What I did NOT independently re-run: the per-AC commands. Those were executed and their output
pasted by the implementing agent, and CI re-ran the full suite on the patchset. Recording the
distinction so the trail says which evidence is first-hand and which is relayed — the completion
verifier gate is the independent check on the criteria themselves.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect (proven, not inferred)

`tests/unit/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` hand-rolls a nested pytest launch
with **no `--basetemp`**, so its child sessions allocate into the SHARED numbered temp root and
destroy other sessions' roots.

`tests/_nested_pytest.py` states the invariant and why it exists: omitting `--basetemp` "lets a
child clean another run's shared numbered temp root", and it "arrived as three separate bugs
before this module existed". This test bypasses that module entirely.

Demonstrated by one serial run of the file, diffing `pytest-of-joeoakhart/`:

```
--- created ---   pytest-2313 pytest-2315 pytest-2316 pytest-2317
--- DELETED ---   pytest-2304 pytest-2310 pytest-2311 pytest-2312
```

Four nested sessions allocated into the shared root and destroyed four other sessions' roots.

## Why the existing guard does not catch it — the more important half

`tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py` detects violations by scanning for the argv triple
`(sys.executable, "-m", "pytest")`. This module spells the same operation as
`(sys.executable, "-c", <script that calls pytest.main>)`.

So it is an **unmarked, undetected violation**: the convention exists, the guard exists, and the
guard's detection shape is narrower than the behaviour it guards. Any future test that drives
pytest through `python -c` gets the same free pass. That is the durable defect — the single test
is just the instance that revealed it.

This is the same family as several other findings in this repo where the CHECK was narrower than
the thing it checked: a CI parity test edited by the very commit that diverged the lanes without
noticing, a drift gate that died on formatting before it ever ran `plan`, an alarm audit that
partitioned on two values of `treat_missing_data` and could not see a third.

## Why it plausibly explains a real flake class

A nested-pytest spawner is DOUBLY exposed: the child's own leak guard can return a non-zero exit,
which surfaces in the parent as a bare `assert completed.returncode == 0` — a failure whose
message says nothing about the actual cause.

A same-family flake was observed while investigating (1 of 3 iterations): `_no_repo_root_leaks`
failing an innocent test on a transient `.rebar/.hlc.state.*.tmp`. That hit a different module
(`test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py`) and the guard's own docstring notes a concurrent external
`rebar` write is indistinguishable there — so it shows the SHAPE is achievable but is not proof
that it caused ticket `undesirous-undiseased-zebu`. Recorded as suggestive, not conclusive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 - `test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` no longer allocates into the shared
      numbered temp root. Route it through `run_nested_pytest`, or pass `--basetemp` under
      `tmp_path` with a reasoned `# nested-pytest-ok:` marker. Prove by diffing
      `pytest-of-<user>/` across a run and showing NO other session's root is deleted.
- [x] AC2 - The uniqueness guard detects a `pytest.main(...)` payload driven through
      `python -c`, not only the `python -m pytest` argv triple. Prove by pointing the guard at the
      pre-fix form of this file and observing it FAIL.
- [x] AC3 - Defect-seeded: reverting AC1 makes AC2's guard go RED. A guard that cannot distinguish
      the fixed form from the broken one has not been shown to work — which is precisely how the
      current guard came to miss this.
- [x] AC4 - A sweep records whether any OTHER test drives pytest through a form the guard cannot
      see. List what was scanned. If others exist, each gets a disposition (fixed here, or its own
      ticket) — silence is not a disposition.

## Non-goals

Not fixing the order-dependent failure reported in `undesirous-undiseased-zebu` — that was
investigated and NOT REPRODUCED, and this ticket does not claim to explain it. Not changing the
nested-pytest convention itself, only its enforcement and this one violator.

file_impact.reason: the guard whose detection shape is narrower than the convention it enforces
AC4 sweep hit: a bare pytest console-script launch with no --basetemp, the second evasion spelling
its docstring enumerates the deliberate exceptions and the invariant the widened guard now enforces

compiled_state.title: A nested-pytest launch driven through python -c evades the uniqueness guard and destroys other sessions' shared temp roots: proven 4-created/4-deleted, and the guard only detects the python -m pytest form
